newsitem.title: INDIA: AT&T to launch India mobile network in Nov.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to launch India mobile network in Nov.

text.p: Birla-AT&T Communications, a joint venture between India's Aditya Birla group and AT&T of the United States, said on Thursday it would launch the first phase of its Indian mobile phone network next month.

The network, for which the venture has won licences in India's richest states of Gujarat and Maharashtra, will mark the end of the first phase of a 51.8 billion rupee ($1.5 billion) project spread over 10 years, the company said in a statement.
When complete the network, also covering the small west coast state of Goa, will be India's largest, with more than one million subscribers, the statement added.
"We are ahead of schedule. We are ahead of the competition," John Legere, AT&T's president for the Asia-Pacific region, told a news conference in New Delhi.
He was referring to his company being the first in India's western region, outside the financial centre of Bombay, to start a mobile phone network.
Legere said the network involved the biggest sole investment in mobile telephones for AT&T outside the United States. "This is a critical investment for us anywhere in the world," he said.

Birla-AT&T's network will cover 10 percent of main district towns in Gujarat and Maharashtra by the end of 1996 and 50 percent by the end of 1998, Rajan Mathew, the joint venture's chief executive, told the news conference.
The network will be the first in India outside the four metropolitan cities of Bombay, Delhi, Calcutta and Madras, an AT&T spokesman said.
Mathew said AT&T would offer seamless roaming to subscribers under its World1 facility and had arranged with mobile phone services firms elsewhere in India to cover 85 percent of the country.
AT&T offcials said the roaming facility was expected to be available by first quarter 1997 when most other mobile telephone networks across India were expected to have started operations.
The Indian government last week approved a rise in the paid-up capital of Birla-AT&T to 12.00 billion rupees ($343 million) from 8.12 billion rupees ($232 million).
The Aditya Birla group holds 51 percent and AT&T wireless Services the rest in the joint venture, which has a 10-year licence period.
Kumar Mangalam Birla, chairman of the Aditya Birla group, said his group looked forward to financing for telecommunication projects from India's long-term lending institutions.
Company officials said they foresaw no financial bottlenecks.
